response.reason: This lens compares each NL-derived atomic contract against the exact closed FCSTM topology (states/transitions at lines 7-18) to detect omitted, wrong-target, or collapsed contracts, malformed default entries, and unauthorized/collision edges. NL-CONTRACT-NL2-INITENTRY-1 is satisfied because the exact InitialState->BrakingState edge (transition:line:13, trigger Brake_Signal_Received) exists and is reachable from the machine root's initial pseudostate ([*]->InitialState at transition:line:12, proved by verify_facts initial-entry check). NL-CONTRACT-NL2-ENDPOINT-1 (BrakingState -> OperationalState on transmission failure) has no corresponding edge in the complete inventory: BrakingState's only outgoing edges are to ClampingState (line:15) and InitialState (line:17); OperationalState is reached only from InitialState (line:14), not BrakingState. This is a complete-inventory absence, yielding an S2 candidate bound to the existing BrakingState/OperationalState state refs. NL-CONTRACT-NL2-ENDPOINT-2 (BrakingState -> InitialState on feedback) IS present exactly as transition:line:17 (BrakingState->InitialState, trigger Signal_Feedback_Sent), so it is satisfied and omitted from candidates. NL-CONTRACT-NL3-ENDPOINT-1 (BrakingState -> ClampingState) is present exactly as transition:line:15, trigger Entering_Clamping_State, so it is satisfied and omitted. The derived guard_disjointness contract cannot be evaluated because ALT-NL2-OPERATIONAL's target relation (BrakingState->OperationalState) does not exist at all in the closed model, and only one of the two alternatives (BrakingState->InitialState) is materialized as an actual edge; since the alternatives are not both live from the same source in the closed model, no exact same-condition collision exists to compare, so guard_disjointness is not raised as a violation but the endpoint absence is the primary candidate for the first alternative. The containment contract (BasicBrakingDevice owning InitialState/BrakingState/OperationalState/ClampingState) is satisfied: reference_inspection_facts and inspection_equivalent_facts show all five leaf states have parent 'llms_emp_feedback_final_0011' (the root wrapper), confirming direct containment; ClampingLoseState is also contained though not named in the contract, which is not a defect. No unauthorized edges are found beyond NL scope (tr_0004/line:15 ClampingLoseState edges are extraneous to NL but exist in source too, not fabricated). No additional derived contracts are needed beyond the supplied set since the misrouted BrakingState->OperationalState absence is already captured by the existing NL-CONTRACT-NL2-ENDPOINT-1 contract; no new causal property is exposed that the NL-only contracts miss.

branches.reason: Behavioral-consequence audit of the closed FCSTM for case 0011. Root reachability and the InitialState->BrakingState/OperationalState edges are exact and satisfied (S2), so the NL2-INITENTRY-1 owner-local edge is satisfied and omitted. The two NL2 alternative-target contracts (ENDPOINT-1 to OperationalState, ENDPOINT-2 to InitialState) both resolve to exact edges from BrakingState in the closed model, but only the InitialState edge exists on the correct source; the OperationalState-target alternative described for BrakingState in NL2 is actually realized only from InitialState (tr_0003/transition:line:14), while BrakingState's real second outgoing edge (besides the clamping edge) targets InitialState via 'Signal Feedback Sent' (transition:line:17), not OperationalState. This creates a wrong-source/wrong-target mismatch for NL-CONTRACT-REF-002. NL3-ENDPOINT-1 (BrakingState -> ClampingState) is exact and satisfied. The derived guard_disjointness contract must be revisited given the corrected topology: BrakingState's two outgoing NL2 alternatives were meant to be distinguishable, but the actual FCSTM only realizes one of them (to InitialState) from BrakingState, while the other (to OperationalState) is actually sourced from InitialState itself, not BrakingState, so the disjointness claim collapses into a wrong-target issue rather than an indistinguishability issue; disjointness contract is therefore not enumerated as a separate candidate here since the two 'alternatives' are not both realized from the same source. The containment contract (root scope owning InitialState/BrakingState/OperationalState/ClampingState) is satisfied: all four states are direct children of the root composite per closed_model_inventory. Behavioral-consequence findings center on: (1) two reachable leaf/dead-end states (ClampingState, ClampingLoseState) with no outgoing transitions, which are terminal design points not covered by any explicit termination contract in the given set, so no termination candidate is emitted absent such a contract; deadlock_freedom is not derivable because no contract establishes an explicit progress obligation for these leaves. (2) Event-consumer coverage for all five events is reachable and satisfied, so no consumer-coverage candidate is needed. The dominant behavioral defect is the NL2-ENDPOINT-1 wrong-target mismatch on BrakingState's failure-alternative, which is preserved as the sole S2-eligible candidate.

stage_receipts.reason: NL1 is descriptive/contextual (names the modeled subject, no independently violable obligation). NL2 establishes an initial entry into the braking state upon receiving a brake signal (actually: transitions from initial state to braking state on brake signal event), an alternative endpoint to an operational state on signal transmission failure, and a return-to-initial-state endpoint on signal feedback sent; these three form a shared-source transition group from the initial/braking state context plus two further endpoints. NL3 establishes an additional endpoint from the braking state to the brake caliper clamping state. Initial-entry semantics: the machine begins in an initial state; the first sentence of NL2 describes the system's transition upon receiving a brake signal from the initial pseudostate to the braking state, which is best modeled as initial_entry (owner=root/BrakingDevice, target=BrakingState) triggered by the brake signal event, alongside a transition group capturing the braking-state alternatives (to operational state, back to initial state) and the further NL3 endpoint (braking to clamping). No cardinality, containment structure, region, or repeated-action obligations are explicitly stated beyond these transition/entry facts, so no additional contracts are manufactured.
